candidates.name: Safaniya Offshore-Onshore Crude Trunkline
candidates.to: onshore processing facility (exact site not named in sources)

evidence.note: Saipem awarded ~$500m EPCI contract (CRPO 156) for a 48-inch crude trunkline, ~65 km offshore + 12 km onshore, from Safaniya oil field to an onshore processing facility, plus subsea tie-ins; fabrication at STAR yard, Dammam.
Confirms same contract scope and 48-inch/65km-offshore+12km-onshore dimensions for Safaniya field trunkline.
Independent trade-press confirmation of the Safaniya trunkline EPCI order under Aramco's long-term offshore framework.

candidates.why_maybe_new: The roster's only Safaniya-linked entries are 'Safaniya-Juaymah Oil Pipeline' (P1958, 198km, dia 46/48, ?->?) and the Khursaniyah/Safiniyah gathering set (P1964-1966, P5169, Safiniyah->Khursaniyah). This newly contracted (Feb 2026) 48-inch, ~77km offshore+onshore trunkline does not match either route/length and appears to be a distinct new transmission segment tied to Safaniya field capacity work — but could conceivably be an expansion/replacement segment of P1958; flagging for consolidator to check against P1958.

candidates.name: Abu Safa Field Crude Trunkline
candidates.to: onshore facility (exact terminus not named in sources)

evidence.note: Saipem awarded EPCI for a ~50 km, 42-inch crude trunkline for the Abu Safa Field, part of a combined ~$500m award under its Aramco long-term agreement.
Trade-press confirmation of the same Abu Safa 42-inch, ~50km crude trunkline EPCI scope, awarded July 2024.

candidates.why_maybe_new: No roster entry names Abu Safa (a field shared 50/50 with Bahrain) as a pipeline endpoint at all — the closest is the unrelated Bahrain-Saudi Oil Pipeline (P0637, Abqaiq->Bapco Refinery). This 42-inch/50km crude trunkline for the Abu Safa field looks like a genuinely new transmission line not covered by any existing PID.

candidates.name: East-West Pipeline (Petroline) Red Sea Capacity Expansion / possible new products pipeline
candidates.sponsor: Saudi Aramco / Saudi government (talks reportedly include Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain)

evidence.note: Saudi Arabia in preliminary talks to add 1-2 million bpd of capacity on the Abqaiq-Yanbu corridor; unclear whether this is an upgrade of existing lines or construction of an entirely new pipeline; one source says plans could include a separate, smaller dedicated pipeline for refined products; talks reportedly involve Kuwait and other neighbors wanting to route oil through Saudi territory to the Red Sea.
Corroborates same reporting: preliminary-stage expansion talks, 1-2 million bpd, motivated by Hormuz risk after the February 2026 Iran conflict.
Same Reuters-sourced story: 2 mmbpd expansion under consideration, cost/timeline unclear, would take years and billions of dollars.

candidates.why_maybe_new: This is explicitly framed as expanding the existing East-West/Petroline corridor (P0551 mainline, P2017 expansion, P5195 Shaybah-Abqaiq capacity expansion segment already on the roster) rather than confirmed as a wholly separate new pipeline — very likely this is just future capacity growth on those existing PIDs. Flagging only because (a) sources explicitly float a second, smaller, dedicated products pipeline as one option, and (b) multi-country through-shipment (Kuwait et al.) could imply new dedicated pipe rather than a simple loop/pump-station upgrade. Status is preliminary talks only (no FID, no contractor, no route/diameter specifics) — consolidator should likely fold this into P0551/P2017/P5195 rather than create a new entry unless firmer details emerge.
